analysis:
Both units are slices of the golden-vector fixture fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (head lines 50177-52071). They hold test data only: request_body, provider_body, template_input, plan hashes and token_ids for the qwen3.6 prompt contract. The file_changes patch excerpt shows the PR altering vectors elsewhere in the file. One hunk adds an additional_context {enable_thinking:false} field, and token counts and chain hashes change correspondingly (803 to 767). That points to a prompt-template or tokenization contract update.

The reviewed slices contain no executable code, secrets, keys, endpoints, authorization logic or attestation logic. They do not change the TB-002 or TB-011 coordinator/provider gates, the A-001 encryption path, or the T-041 cache boundary directly. They only encode expected tokenization and cache-block hashes, and the prompt_contract_id in the reviewed head slices is unchanged. Partial patch visibility (excerpt incomplete) means I only saw the first hunk.

Integration questions for the next pass: (1) Confirm the matching Swift/Go prompt-contract and template code changes. These are not in this batch. Check that the provider and coordinator derive the same prompt_contract_id and chain hashes, and that the prefix-cache keying (T-041) includes the contract id. If the template changes but the id does not, cached KV from different templates could be shared across scopes. (2) The head fixtures show prompt_contract_id 4b92f7... on vectors, but I cannot see whether it changed from base for the hunks that were altered. No concrete regression is established from the supplied evidence.
